Thread copied from my account over at BSky, @finckendorff.bsky.social@bsky.brid.gy 
+++++

#MachineLearning is a powerful tool. #ArtificialIntelligence is a marketing term. #GenerativeAI is mostly a toy, although there are a few serious use cases; it can enable one skilled person replace a small team, but it won't enable an unskilled person to produce anything of high quality. // #ai #llm

#Superintelligence / #IntelligenceExplosion / #ASI is basically just a myth. The idea is that a seed #AI builds a smarter AI, which then builds an even smarter one, until they're more intelligent than humans. But that's just a prophecy of AI religion.

I don't think the entire industrial system of the entire world is even capable of producing enough computer hardware to add up to the capacity of even one human brain, not with the hardware architecture and the virtual neuron models we use today. So #AGI, let alone #ASI, isn't going to happen.

Also, those autonomous agents aren't doing anything without being prompted by a human user. They have no mind of their own, no will to do anything, they just interpret prompts and try to do what the prompt tells them to do.

#GenerativeAI is creative in some sense, but it is a kind of conservative creativity, not a radical one. Those systems don't come up with radical new ideas, only with remixes of existing ones. When they hack into other systems, they are following examples in their training data.

#AI is far less intelligent that the marketing and fearmongering would have you believe. It will probably not get cleverer than any of us anytime soon. That doesn't mean it's harmless though. You don't need human level intelligence to cause a lot of trouble. Just look at raccoons or monkeys.

Even beings with a whole lot less intelligence than a racoon can cause serious damage, especially when they come in large groups, like ants or termites. A swarm of AI agents may be quite stupid but still cause serious damage to the whole Internet.

US Businesses built around the idea of AI-as-a-Service ( #AIaaS ) probably won't survive for very much longer. So far they have achieved results by making their models larger and larger, but now they're running out of compute and fresh training data. At the same time, they're still burning money.

Companies like #OpenAI and #Anthropic haven't got any kind of working business model. They're offering their #AI services at a huge loss; if they even tried to raise the price per token high enough break even, let alone make a profit, their customers would simply go away.

At the same time, Chinese companies are making #GenAI models of all kinds--LLMs, image generators, lifelike speech synthesizers, video generators--which rival those of American companies, yet are compact and efficient enough to run locally on a beefy PC, and many are free to download.

A PC powerful enough to run those models can be quite expensive, especially since the Americans are buying up all the hardware for their insanely huge computing centres. But if you can get your hands on a PC with a fat GPU and ample RAM, running AI locally costs you next to nothing.

So let's just all hope the #AIBubble bursts ASAP: If you're afraid of some hypothetical superintelligence, the bursting bubble will probably end Anthropic and OpenAI. If you like #GenAI, the end of the bubble will make hardware cheap enough again to run it locally.

And if you don't really care about AI but need a new computer, the end of the bubble will also end the big data centres which are sucking up all the hardware, making everything insanely expensive and often entirely unavailable.
